252f3c5991dc48c1d0205d39cea73b57730dbf1a: La Bresse-Hohneck is the highest and largest resort in the Vosges, sitting at 920 m above sea level at the foot of the Hohneck (1,363 m). Its 21 km of runs offer some of the most reliable snow cover in the massif and a wide variety of slopes to suit every level, from beginners to confident skiers. A family resort very popular with people from Alsace and Lorraine, it appeals with its friendly atmosphere and affordable prices. Two ski schools operate at the snow front. 253da9b8ca3a2112d0af24ef66bde7edf0a5a158: Bürchen-Moosalp is a small, low-key resort: 25 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Bürchen-Moosalp's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2532 m and a village at 1476 m, snow cover at Bürchen-Moosalp is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but conditions recover quickly once the first serious snowfalls arrive. The overall budget for a stay at Bürchen-Moosalp is clearly high: a day lift pass at 56€, plus mountain accommodation and restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. That is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you set off. In short: Bürchen-Moosalp doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
